evidence.note: Before any overlay appears, the context diagram is already blurred so heavily that no label, node or flow is readable; only faint coloured smudges and a vague legend row remain.
Same heavy blur at the small size; the diagram reads as an indistinct grey/blue patch with nothing in focus below the title.
White insight card with soft drop shadow floats crisply above the blurred diagram; the card has clear focus.
Three opaque cards cover the diagram almost entirely; only faint smudges show between and below cards, so the context is no longer recognisable.
Cards fill the body width; the underlying diagram is effectively invisible.

rationale: The cards themselves have clear focus via shadow and opacity, but the frost on the context is so heavy that the diagram is unrecognisable even at step 0, before any overlay needs separating from it. By step 3 the opaque cards hide what little remains, so the context is lost rather than softened, matching the fail descriptor's 'effects so heavy the context is lost'.
